lines: {name}. You're the one filling in a Vellum for Halcyon Vess.
Isolde Kerrow. I direct the Stillwater Concord, which mostly means I sign things.
He writes to this office every week. Careful letters. Good numbers in them.
I read all of them. I have answered none.
I'd rather tell you why to your face than let you work it out from the filing.
Seventy years ago the Hollow Sea turned over and took a town called Old Tidefall.
One night. Two hundred and forty people. My brother was one. I was six.
Dr. Vess would like us to observe the Turning. Record it. Understand it.
He's right that it is the greater science. He is usually right.
I would like to stop it.
Not delay it. Not survive it. Stop it, and never have that conversation again.
You've walked the west arm. Streams dropping, herds refusing the bridge.
Everyone tells you that is frightening. It isn't. That is the sea being held.
That is us. That is the work going right.
Go on to Brackwater. Take your Seals, they're a fine thing to have.
And the next time Vess writes to you about the Turning, ask him one question.
Ask him what he intends to say to the next Old Tidefall.
The soundings pinned above it are not. Somebody has ringed the west face twice.
